ClientResponses.Response: Hello, thank you for being a longtime Weber fan! Our sincerest apologies for the trouble with flare-ups. As this is a normal byproduct of grilling over live fire, and while they can never be eliminated entirely, there are steps we can take to reduce them. If you are using a marinade, we suggest getting as much excess of liquid off as possible before putting the food on the grill. We would also recommend waiting at least 5-10 minutes before trying to add any sauce on your food. We are glad to hear you are keeping the grill clean, as this significantly reduces the flare-ups. We have additional tips here: https://www.weber.com/US/en/blog/tips-techniques/preventing-flare-ups/weber-31145.html. This grill does carry a 10-year warranty, so if you notice any holes rusting through the flavorizer bars, please do not hesitate to reach our support team. They will be happy to assist you with this. Thank you!
ClientResponses.Name: Weber grills

Results.ReviewText: Love Weber products and have owned Weber grills for decades. I purchased my Weber Spirit II to replace a larger version that lasted for 15 years. I downsized due to price and being an empty nester. The second time I grilled (hamburgers) I had several large-sized flare-ups during the grilling process. It scared me. I don’t recall having flare ups to this degree with my former Weber grills. I now clean/hand wash the flavor bars, drip pan and grates every time before grilling to diminish the flare ups. I also wipe down the interior sides and bottom of the grill with a soapy cloth to clean grease/marinade drippings. There isn’t an issue with chicken, yet I grilled steaks on two different occasions resulting in big flare ups. I realize the fat content of meat causes flare ups, yet never had problems grilling rib-eyes before. Because the flavor bars and depth of the grill is closer together/more compact, I think this is a contributing factor of the flare ups. I’ve also noticed the flavor grills the enamel has bubbled, pitted and in a few area has rust. Never an issue with my past Weber grills. I have concerns the flavor bars will have to be replaced sooner rather than later. The grill has a cover and kept cleaned so unsure why I’m already experiencing some problems with the grill. The only time I’ll grill burgers or steaks is when my son comes home as the large flare ups scare me. My son said “mom have a fire extinguisher close by if I’m not there.” I grew up in California with many fires so I have a healthy respect/minor phobia with fire.
Results.Title: Don’t like the flare ups.......

Results.ReviewText: After years of buying cheaper bends of LP grills only to junk them 3 or 4 years later when they rusted out, I decided I could do without. They were difficult to cook well with and results were inconsistent anyway, so I didn’t use them very much and didn’t really miss outside grilling.  Then, this summer we rented a house for vacation and it had a Weber grill.  I was amazed at the difference. I thought all grills were the same but, boy, was I wrong!  For the first time I cooked to perfection, not just once or twice but consistently.  I decided to invest in a Weber as soon as I returned home.  I bought online direct from the manufacturer and the difference was apparent the moment it arrived - it was heavy!  The packaging itself was a piece of engineering. It was like all the pieces had been born and grown inside the box in perfect placement. If Apple made grills this is how they would arrive packaged! The instructions were legible and easy to follow and every piece fit together absolutely perfectly without once having to force a hole to line up or finagle a piece to fit in place.  The quality of the whole experience was remarkable.  I have grilled more in the past two weeks of owning my Weber than I did in a whole season previously. The results have been excellent and consistent and I have a feeling this Weber is going to last me for years and years.
Results.Title: I thought I was done with outside grilling....

Results.ReviewText:
I have heard for years that Weber grills are well worth the extra cost, yet foolishly bought other brands that were on their way to becoming junk after one or two seasons.  Then it was a matter of paying more than I should have to replace rusted parts for several more years.  Fortunately, my neighbor told me about the quality and longevity of his Weber.  

This 2-burner Weber Spirit II is studier than any grill I have ever used, and I expect it will last a long time.  I also bought a Weber cover, and it is every bit as rugged, and seems likely to last for many years.  I guess time will tell, but there’s another matter I never considered much:  this Weber cooks better than any grill I’ve owned.  The cooking grates alone are better than I’d have imagined.  I just treat them like a good cast iron skillet and keep them well seasoned.  Is there REALLY a difference in the food?  You bet there is!  

My only regret is that I waited way too long to do this!  I wish I had just invested the extra bucks and bought a Weber years ago.  I’d have saved a lot of money in the long run.  

One other smart move I made was to buy the grill at our local Ace Hardware, who had a special deal where they assembled the grill for free, AND they assembled it properly.  I read way too many reviews where people bought grills from big box stores like Home Depot where they preassembled ( more like slapped together ) by people who were barely out of their teens and who couldn’t care less about the quality.  Then, the grills often sit out on the floor, if not outside, and get filthy.  If nothing else, get your grill in the box and assemble it yourself, if you can.  If you don’t believe me, go to your local home improvement store and inspect the grills chained together sitting outside.

Another Suggestion: get a container of disposable wipes for cleaning stainless steel.  There are several stainless steel surfaces on the grill, and stainless can be a pain to clean.  After reading all about using microfiber cloths and special cleaning products, I decided it was all too much bother.  I got the wipes at Walmart, and they come in a plastic container just like disinfectant wipes.  It’s easy to keep it in a box on my deck, use one or two wipes before I put the cover back on, then I don’t have to launder a microfiber rag.  The grill sparkles, it’s effortless, and fresh wipes are always at the ready.

Anyhow, for anyone looking at grills- save yourself the grief and quit wasting money- just buy a Weber.
Results.Title: The Quality Is Worth The Price

The last grill I had was a cheaper brand and I operated it for years, replacing almost every part on it at least once. Results.ReviewText:
I have owned various single burner grills for the last several years. After looking around I decided to go with a more long term solution. Having owned 2 Weber kettle grills, one for 17 years, and a newer one for the last 10 years, I gave Weber a hard look.  The construction appears to be robust, especially in the main body. That is mainly what made me go with the Weber. My real review comments will be several years from now after we have some mileage on the grill.

In the now: this thing rocks!  It gets hot quick, and is easy to control. I do a lot of indirect heat grilling and that is working great with this grill. 

As for size, this size suits me - go to a store and determine if you need a bigger one. As I said I also own a Weber charcoal grill. One reason is that I sometimes like to grill with the briquets; the other is that the charcoal grill offers me the occasional required extra capacity for gatherings.

Results.ReviewText:
- The worst packed product ever. Please buy some Apple stuff to see how a premium product is supposed to be packaged! I’d fire the engineer who designed the packaging for this grill!
- Lowering left shelf means water sits in it if it rains: a mosquito breeding spot. Forces user to keep shelf up.
- Both shelves should fold down and drain fully too!
- Stick on a chain is stupidly attached in a plastic bag, which user assumes is a part they will need. Once out, bag is destroyed and stick is awkwardly and ugly and hung from the unit. Again: fire engineer! - Bottom shelf is useless. Needs a watertight cabinet for storage.
- Design of grease tray is sloppy and terrible. Should be a bottle shape to carry and empty, be dishwasher safe and attach easier.
- This unit could easily be adapted for remote temp control and sensing using an app. A missed profit opportunity. Instead they sell lousy covers and aluminum slop trays. Time for the future Weber!
- Rain water does seem to get under the closed lid. Concerning if grilling and it is raining. 
- Because of these and a few other flaws, like vague and imprecise temp control knobs, this is more like a $265 grill. Not a $400 premium grill.
Results.Title: Grills nice but, many obvious simple design flaws

Results.OriginalProductName: Spirit II E-210 Gas Grill (Liquid Propane)
Results.ReviewText:
What a nice grill. I'm very happy that I chose this grill. The way the propane tank hangs on the scale on the side is awesome. Very easy to remove and reinstall the propane tank, plus the scale shows the weight and remaining fuel left. A shelf on the bottom. A temperature gauge on the lid. A well designed drip tray and they offer aluminum insert pans to keep it easy to keep clean. 

Starting the burners is also easy with the button to ignite. Easy to clean grates after cooking. They also offer a Bluetooth temperature probe that there is a knock out on the right side upper shelf to support it and a good look, instead of just hanging somewhere. It works as it should, I enjoyed it.

The over all quality is what make Weber one of the best made grills on the market. Good wheels, the left upper shelf can lower and the cool to touch handle is smart in design. The price was in line with other grills and cheaper priced than others. It doesn't have a side burner (I never really used one when I had one). If there was something I didn't like I'd post it. I do recommend the Srpirit II E-210 gas Grill. Even though this is a 2 burner grill, I was able to easily cook for 5 people. 

I absolutely recommend this grill or any of the similar Spirit grill choices. The difference is amount of burners, the quality is the same. See it, touch it and you'll know it's quality. What a good looking quality grill.
Results.Title: Perfect! I love my Weber E-210 grill.

Results.OriginalProductName: Spirit II E-210 Gas Grill (Liquid Propane)
Results.ReviewText: I bought this 2 burner Spirit recently as my other Spirit (purchased in the early 2000’s) was needing new parts & I was ready for a new toy. Man-Oh-Man, has grill technology come a long way. This grill actually has real temperature control. After about a month of use, I have experienced zero flare ups. The cast-iron grills are a significant improvement over the porcelain coated steel in my previous model. I mainly grill beef (steaks & burgers) but did have a chance to grill some chicken wings recently. I was worried a bit about flare ups, but none happened. Next time I will probably increase the heat (I wasn’t sure what to expect). I highly recommend.
Results.Title: Awesome grill
